images.caption: Figure 1:Compared with full-step sampling (a), Speculative Forcing treats intermediate token estimates as drafts, accepts those that have converged, and refines only the rest (b), achieving comparable quality with fewer denoising steps and higher throughput (c).

Figure 2:Token-wise convergence during denoising.We visualize latent differences between each chunk’skk-step prediction and the baseline four-step output.
(a) In video generation, background and object regions that remain similar to history tend to converge early, while other regions continue to change. (b) In world generation, previously observed regions often converge early, whereas newly revealed regions tend to require further denoising.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparisons on video generation and world modeling.Both our head and training-free verifiers preserve visual quality comparable to the four-step baseline without visibly increasing quality drift over the illustrated rollouts on our benchmark.

Figure 5:Qualitative ablations of verification and commitment granularity.Our learned verifier handles distortions that challenge training-free verification.
Premature chunk-wise acceptance propagates errors to later chunks, while motion-based verification struggles to distinguish camera-induced changes from distortions.
